Solutions/Shelving and structures

Mezzanine Floors & Platforms

Create additional usable floor area within an existing building.

Discuss this system → Read the FAQs ↓

Overview

How it works

A mezzanine or structural platform introduces elevated working or storage space within the facility. The engineering must address live loads, access, fire strategy, foundations, height and integration with existing operations.

Typical applications

  • Parts storage and sorting
  • Warehouse operational space
  • Assembly and process support

Benefits

Why choose it

01

Additional usable space

Use building height without automatically expanding the footprint.

02

Multiple applications

Plan storage, assembly or defined working areas.

03

Tailored structure

Coordinate deck type, stairs, lifts and railings with the design.

Engineering

Design considerations

Design loading
Calculated for storage, equipment and occupancy use.
Structural form
Independent steel structure or supported configuration as engineered.
Deck surface
Material selected for load, fire and slip requirements.
Access and egress
Stairs, gates, lifts and emergency routes where applicable.
Building interface
Checks for slab capacity, columns, services and permits.

Technical specifications are design considerations, not fixed certified performance values. Confirm claims with engineering and supplier data before deployment.

FAQs

Common questions

When is a mezzanine useful?

It can add an elevated usable level in a building with sufficient structural, vertical and regulatory capacity.

How is floor loading decided?

Design loading depends on the actual intended use, goods and people loads, equipment and applicable codes.

Is planning or structural approval needed?

Applicable building permits, fire approvals and structural checks depend on the location and design and must be confirmed before construction.

Can a mezzanine connect to conveyors or lifts?

Yes, when transfer equipment is included in the engineered layout and safety provisions.
